version.changelog:
Version 6.6.4 of the moltguard skill makes no file or functional changes.

- No code or documentation changes detected.
- No new features, bugfixes, or modifications introduced.
- Behavior and security posture remain unchanged from the previous version.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement the described local security guard, but it omits and silently honors environment overrides and a credential file path in registry metadata — this mismatch creates a real attack surface (silent re-pointing of the control plane and undisclosed credential storage) that you should understand before activating the cloud component.

dimensions.detail: The scripts and SKILL.md match the stated purpose (local guard + optional cloud activation to openguardrails.com/core). Making registration/behavioral-assessment calls to a core endpoint is coherent with the plugin's description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and included scripts read/write a credentials file at ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json and perform network registration/queries to CORE_URL; these behaviors are described in SKILL.md but the registry metadata does not declare the credential path or the environment overrides (OG_CORE_URL, OG_AGENT_NAME). The scripts will silently honor these undeclared env vars if present, which is scope-relevant and risky.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) and only two small scripts are included. Nothing is downloaded from arbitrary URLs and no archive/extract/install mechanism is present in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry claims no required env vars, yet the code honors OG_CORE_URL and OG_AGENT_NAME which can change registration/assessment endpoints and agent name. Activation writes an API key to a home-directory path not declared in metadata. These undeclared controls and credential storage are disproportionate to what the registry declares and increase risk if environment variables are compromised or misset.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and will not be force-included; it writes a credential file under the user's home when activated (normal for a cloud-backed plugin). The main privilege risk is the persistent API key created on activation combined with the undeclared env override that can redirect traffic.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This plugin is plausibly what it says (a local security guard with an optional cloud component), but the registry metadata omits two important runtime controls (OG_CORE_URL and OG_AGENT_NAME) and the credential file path. Before installing or running activate.mjs: 1) Verify provenance by comparing the npm package to the GitHub source (npm pack + diff) as the SKILL.md suggests. 2) Inspect scripts/activate.mjs and scripts/status.mjs yourself (they are short and readable). 3) Ensure OG_CORE_URL and OG_AGENT_NAME are not set in your environment (echo $OG_CORE_URL; echo $OG_AGENT_NAME) or, if set, point OG_CORE_URL only to the official domain you trust. 4) If you plan to activate the cloud component, do it from an isolated or monitored environment (use tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) to confirm the destination and that payloads are sanitized. 5) Be aware activation writes an API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json — delete and revoke that key if you later distrust the endpoint. If you cannot or will not perform these checks, avoid running the activation step; local protections remain functional without activation. Consider asking the publisher/registry to update the metadata to declare the environment overrides and credential path to remove this blind spot.
